parts.label: a
parts.ask: \(\mathrm{f}(x) = \dfrac{7x\mathrm{e}^x}{\sqrt{\mathrm{e}^{3x} - 2}}\), \(x > \ln\sqrt[3]{2}\). Show that \(\mathrm{f}'(x) = \dfrac{7\mathrm{e}^x\left(\mathrm{e}^{3x}(2 - x) + Ax + B\right)}{2(\mathrm{e}^{3x} - 2)^{\frac{3}{2}}}\), where \(A\) and \(B\) are constants to be found.

steps.why: Chain rule: the inside \(\mathrm{e}^{3x} - 2\) differentiates to \(3\mathrm{e}^{3x}\).

parts.label: b
parts.ask: Hence show that the \(x\) coordinates of the turning points of the curve are solutions of \(x = \dfrac{2\mathrm{e}^{3x} - 4}{\mathrm{e}^{3x} + 4}\).

steps.why: \(\mathrm{f}'(x) = 0\), and \(7\mathrm{e}^x \neq 0\): only the bracket can be zero.
Gather the \(x\) terms on one side, then factor out \(x\).

parts.label: c
parts.ask: The equation has two positive roots \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), with \(\beta > \alpha\). Diagram 1 shows part of the S-shaped curve \(y = \dfrac{2\mathrm{e}^{3x} - 4}{\mathrm{e}^{3x} + 4}\) and the line \(y = x\), crossing at \(\alpha\) (below 1) and \(\beta\) (above 1). Draw a staircase diagram to show that \(x_{n+1} = \dfrac{2\mathrm{e}^{3x_n} - 4}{\mathrm{e}^{3x_n} + 4}\) with \(x_1 = 1\) can be used to approximate \(\beta\).

steps.text: From \(x = 1\), go up to the curve, across to \(y = x\), up to the curve again, and repeat.
steps.why: Between \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) the curve is above the line, so the steps climb.

parts.answerText: At least two steps rising to the right, ending where the curve meets \(y = x\) at \(\beta\): the iteration converges to \(\beta\).

check.answers: sketch: staircase from x = 1 converging to beta

parts.label: d(i)
parts.ask: Using the iteration formula with \(x_1 = 1\), find \(x_2\) to 3 decimal places.

steps.why: Use the full calculator value each time (the ANS key).
Stop when the values agree to 3 d.p.

parts.label: e
parts.ask: Using a suitable interval and a suitable function that should be stated, show that \(\alpha = 0.432\) to 3 decimal places.

steps.why: State the function: \(\mathrm{h}(x) = 0\) at \(\alpha\). Test the bounds 0.4315 and 0.4325.

steps.text: The sign changes, and h is continuous on \([0.4315, 0.4325]\), so \(\alpha\) lies in this interval.
steps.why: Say continuous: without it the graph could jump the axis.
